lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
Date of birth: 5 Feb 1998 | Nationality: Singaporean
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved close efficiency by 40% by automating reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Wrote the variance commentary for the monthly board pack, explaining each line more than 5% off budget.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Reported a 45% group EBITDA margin by adding the EBITDA margins of the three business units.
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Owned the credit reviews for the small-business loan book and the watch list the lending officers used.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; the findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Wrote the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Tested the valuation's sensitivity: a 1-point change in the discount rate moved the share value from USD 52 to USD 44.
- Shared the model and a two-page note with the university investment club, which used it in its spring pitch.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Built an 18-month cash forecast for a USD 600M business, holding error to about 4% and freeing USD 40M to repay debt early.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Bloomberg Terminal
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuaton, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: The résumé includes date of birth and nationality, personal details readers are not expected to weigh.
items.because: They take space and attention from qualifications relevant to the role.

items.says: The dated Student Investment Fund entry adds less to the current professional story than later work.
items.because: Keeping the full 2018–2019 entry may give older, less relevant material too much space.

items.says: Education appears before the relevant work history.
items.because: With several years of relevant experience, placing Education first delays the professional evidence recruiters are likely to seek.

items.says: The 40% efficiency gain has no baseline or comparison period.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what changed by 40% or over what period.

items.says: The repeated “by” makes the sentence awkward.
items.because: It makes the relationship between the gain and the automation less clear.

items.says: The shared rules are presented without stating what they improved.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether the template changed a capital decision or improved the planning process.

items.says: The board-pack commentary does not say what it helped the board or finance team do.
items.because: Its effect on actions or decisions remains unknown.

items.says: The valuation mismatches free cash flow to equity with WACC.
items.because: FCFE is discounted at the cost of equity; WACC is used for free cash flow to the firm.

items.says: The valuation method is given without an estimate or other stated result.
items.because: A reader cannot gauge the result or its significance from the method alone.

items.says: Adding business-unit EBITDA margins does not calculate a group EBITDA margin.
items.because: The group margin is combined EBITDA divided by combined revenue, or a revenue-weighted average of unit margins.

items.says: The margin is reported without saying what it informed.
The calculation explanation follows the figure.
The debt-repayment result appears late rather than leading the Stonebridge experience.
“Owned” frames the credit reviews as a responsibility rather than a concrete action.
items.because: It does not tell the reader what you did.

items.says: The watch-list explanation adds words without clarifying the work.
The credit reviews have no portfolio scale or outcome.
items.because: Their scope and effect are unclear.

items.says: The historical review does not establish that changed thresholds caused approvals to rise without increasing early defaults.
items.because: The claim requires observed results under the changed policy and a credible comparison.

items.says: The line’s strongest work does not lead the Crescent Bank entry.
The market price used for the 6% comparison has no measurement date.
The “1-point change” lacks a baseline, a clear unit and the direction associated with each share value.
items.because: A reader cannot tell which scenario produced each value or reproduce the comparison.

items.says: The deliverables do not identify the analysis or model feature the club used.
items.because: The project gives little evidence of the valuation skill or insight contributed.

items.says: The “which used it” clause leaves unclear what the club used.
“Supported” and “financial reporting and analysis” do not identify the work performed.
items.because: The bullet gives little evidence of the candidate’s contribution.

items.says: The FP&A bullet does not say what the work achieved.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what effect it had.

items.says: The committee’s use of the report is buried, and “at every meeting” is wordy.
The forecast repeats the distinctive Stonebridge achievement under a different role and date.
items.because: The matching horizon, business scale, error and debt repayment make the work appear misattributed.

items.says: The forecast error is imprecise and has no stated calculation basis or comparison.
items.because: “About 4%” makes the accuracy claim hard to assess.

items.says: The forecast method and scope come before the debt-repayment result and accuracy.
items.because: A scanning reader may give the strongest outcomes less attention.

items.says: The Student Investment Fund entry mixes generic FP&A and cash-forecast work with fund-performance work.
items.because: The bullets do not establish the same connection and make the entry read as unrelated work.

items.says: “Valuaton” is misspelled in the Methods skills line.
items.because: The visible typo can distract readers and make the document appear insufficiently checked.
